newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start higher, BIS suspended.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start higher, BIS suspended.

text.p: French shares started higher on Monday on the back of a fresh record on Wall Street but some technical analysts warned for a decline later on, dealers said.
A stronger franc and rises on the bond market also supported shares. London climbed to a record and Frankfurt also rose.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.74 points or 0.34 percent at 2,314.69 at 0906 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,316.5 from 2,305 on Friday's close.
Shares in temp agency BIS were suspended pending a statement, the SBF stock exchanges association said.
GAN, down 0.37 percent at 107 francs, is set to ask for state capital increase of seven to 10 billion francs, according to the Les Echos financial newspaper.

France Telecom, slated for partial privatisation around April, will have a share capital of 25 billion francs when it starts its new life as a corporation on January 1, according to a decree publsihed in the Journal Officiel.
Accor, up 1.92 percent at 636 francs, expected to take over the company that runs the Dax thermal station.
Renault, up 0.36 percent at 111.40 francs, in talks to buy lorry business of Finland's Sisu Oy, Sisu said.
